resources.string: This app never replaces your keyboard automatically. Enable Chimera Terminal Keyboard only if you want its shell keys, or keep your own keyboard - both work.
Uses a real su from Magisk, KernelSU or an engineering ROM when one exists.
Runs a full Linux userland as fake uid 0. Works on unrooted devices, including Amazon Fire tablets.
Keeps sandbox sessions alive while you are elsewhere.
Install the real Termux userland so pkg, apt, bash, git, python, ssh and the rest of the Termux repository work inside a sandbox. Binaries are Android-native and run directly on the device.
Termux binaries expect the path /data/data/com.termux/files/usr. This app runs them through proot, which binds that path onto the sandbox. Install proot first.
Once installed: pkg update, pkg install git, pkg install python, apt install openssh, and so on.
Disable or remove preinstalled apps without a PC and without touching the system partition. Requires Shizuku (ADB-level) or root.

Shizuku runs an ADB-identity process on the device. On Android 11+ you can start it from the phone itself using Developer options and Wireless debugging - no PC needed. Install Shizuku, start it, then tap Grant.
Protected system component - blocked for safety
No ADB-level or root access. Listing works; disabling and removing do not.
What this can and cannot do

With Shizuku or root this removes apps for user 0, exactly like adb shell pm uninstall --user 0. The system partition is untouched, so the device still boots, updates still work, and every action can be restored. With neither, the app opens the system screen so you can disable or remove the app yourself.

Android does not let an ordinary app disable or remove another app, so this app cannot do it directly for %1$s. You have two options.

Open the system screen for this app, where you can force stop it, disable it or remove updates.

Or read how to turn on direct removal, which needs no PC on Android 11 or newer.
How to turn on direct removal
Opened the system screen for this app.

Direct removal needs the same access a computer would use over USB. You have three ways to get it, and none of them needs a PC on Android 11 or newer.

1. Root. If your device is rooted, this app uses su automatically.

2. Shizuku. Install the Shizuku app, open Developer options, turn on Wireless debugging, then start Shizuku from inside the Shizuku app. Come back here and tap Grant. This runs an ADB-identity process on the device itself.

3. The system screens. Open App info for any app and disable or uninstall it by hand. This always works and needs no extra app.

The app tells you which of these is active at the top of this screen.
